title: How To Build Your Own 3D Studio With Clo - Murph Studio User Story
description:
Carol Barbosa, founder of @murphstudio_ shares how she left one of Brazil's largest fashion retailers to build her own 3D studio and help brands transform their product development process with CLO.

"When I discovered CLO, it immediately clicked because it brings together the best of both worlds: fashion and technology."

Discover how Carol transformed her career and how digital workflows are changing the future of product development.
transcript: Hi, I'm Carol, from Murph, and today I'll show you how I transformed my traditional fashion career into digital fashion, optimizing the company's resources and using the best software in the industry, Clou. I graduated in fashion and worked for great fashion designers in Brazil since the beginning of college. I've always been a very questioning person, especially about the industry's processes and the impact of fashion. In addition, I've always liked technology, new programs and graphic design software. When I met Clou, I identified with her because she brought together the best in the world, fashion, technology and sustainability. It was then that the career transition happened. I left one of the biggest retailers in the country to create my own 3D studio, focusing on helping customers solve problems they see up close every day, such as the reduction in product development time with the validation of digital pieces, with 3D, through Clou. For Murph, who deals with retail, Clou is our main tool for strategic efficiency. With Clou, digitalization of modeling allows real-time testing, which took weeks to be seen on a physical screen, is now approved in minutes or hours on the screen, saving time and resources during the processes. And in the Closet is where the magic of management happens. You don't need to convert the files, or download or send by email or WhatsApp. Everything can happen in an integrated way on the platform itself. And don't worry, if you send the correct version, everything is always updated. At Murph, we've already developed all the pieces of the customer's collection digitally, even before the product is made. Without Clou and Closet, it would be impossible to maintain this level of precision and speed. Our customers' focus varies according to the goal, from product validation to campaigns for launch of collections or marketing activations. Before this technology, it was a month of development, excess of physical prototypes, and fragmented communication, which was a challenge for the entire team, which generated waste and high costs for the brands. But it's not just 3D. Murph meets each customer in a unique way, understanding the processes of each company and how we can act to optimize the brand's time to market. Together with our partners, we develop the best solutions for the companies we serve. Over time, our portfolio and client base has grown increasingly. And with that, I was able to live a dream that Carol couldn't even imagine. To have Clou not only as another marketing software, but as a complete partner, a support, and a team, which also strengthens us as suppliers. I'm sure Clou will always bring us the best solutions and formats for the digital fashion segment. CLOU. CLOU. CLOU. CLOU. CLOU. Start now and transform your creative process. CLOU. CLOU. CLOU. CLOU.
markdown_content: ## Murph’s Digital Fashion Studio (Carol’s Career Transition) This section introduces Carol from Murph and explains how she shifted from traditional fashion to digital fashion using Clou (and its platform features). It also frames the motivation: optimizing resources while improving speed, validation, and sustainability. Carol, a fashion graduate, worked for major fashion designers in Brazil since early in college. She describes herself as highly questioning—especially about how fashion industry processes affect outcomes—and as someone who has always been interested in technology, new programs, and graphic design software. Her transition happened after she met Clou, which she connects to a combination of fashion, technology, and sustainability. The move was also personal and strategic: she left one of the largest retailers in the country to create her own 3D studio. Her focus is helping customers solve problems they see up close every day, particularly those related to reducing product development time through digital validation of pieces using 3D workflows within Clou. For Murph, which supports retail, Clou is positioned as the main tool for strategic efficiency. Carol emphasizes that Clou is not treated as “just another marketing software,” but as a complete partner—supporting the studio as a team and strengthening Murph in its role as a supplier. She also expresses confidence that Clou will continue bringing solutions and formats for the digital fashion segment. --- ## Clou for 3D Digitalization: Faster Validation and Real-Time Testing This section details how Murph uses Clou to digitize modeling, enabling real-time testing and faster approvals compared to physical screens and prototypes. It highlights time/resource savings as a core outcome. Carol explains that with Clou, digitalization of modeling enables real-time testing. Previously, it took weeks to view and validate changes on a physical screen. With the Clou 3D workflow, approvals happen in minutes or hours directly on the screen. This reduces time and resources across the development and validation process. She also contrasts the “before” and “after” states in practical terms: prior workflows involved a month of development, excess physical prototypes, and fragmented communication among the team. This fragmentation created waste and increased costs for brands. By moving validation earlier and into digital review, Murph aims to reduce those inefficiencies while maintaining precision and speed. Carol also notes that Murph has already developed all pieces of a customer’s collection digitally—even before the product is made. She states that without Clou and Closet, it would be impossible to maintain the same level of precision and speed at Murph’s scale. --- ## Closet Platform Workflow: No File Conversion, No Email/WhatsApp Exchange This section explains how Closet supports an integrated workflow so teams don’t need to convert files or transfer them through email or messaging apps. It also covers how “sending the correct version” keeps everything updated. Carol describes Closet as the place where “the magic of management happens,” because it enables integrated collaboration on the platform itself. Teams do not need to convert files or download and send assets by email or WhatsApp. Instead, everything can happen within the platform environment. A key operational caveat is version control: Carol notes that if the correct version is sent, everything remains updated. This implies that Closet is designed to reduce manual coordination overhead and prevent mismatches between file versions during the digital fashion review process. --- ## Customer Use Cases: Validation, Launch Campaigns, and Marketing Activations This section clarifies how Murph’s clients use Clou/3D outputs for different goals beyond product development. It includes examples tied to collection launches and marketing activations. Carol explains that customer focus varies depending on the objective. The work can support: - **Product validation** (confirming pieces digitally before physical production) - **Campaigns for launching collections** - **Marketing activations** She positions the digital workflow as useful across both development and promotion, enabling teams to move faster from creation to market-facing activities. --- ## Murph’s Service Model: Optimizing Time to Market with Partners This section describes Murph’s broader approach to digital fashion services, emphasizing tailored processes for each company and collaboration with partners. It connects technology adoption to improved time-to-market. Carol states that Murph goes beyond 3D by meeting each customer uniquely. Murph understands the processes of each company and works on how to act to optimize the brand’s **time to market**. Together with partners, Murph develops solutions suited to the companies they serve. Carol also notes that Murph’s portfolio and client base have grown over time, reinforcing the value of having Clou as more than a tool—she describes it as a long-term partner that supports Murph’s ability to deliver digital fashion solutions. ---
